market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: Acquiring any Greenland territory would require a binding transfer of sovereignty or exclusive jurisdiction, strongly opposed by both Denmark and Greenland. No US administration is actively pursuing this, and the 2026 deadline makes a forced acquisition against a NATO ally exceptionally unlikely. The 14.5% implied probability massively overstates a negligible tail risk.
evidence_points: Denmark and Greenland promptly rejected Trump's 2019 purchase offer and have shown no interest in ceding territory.
The resolution requires binding agreement or use of force; a voluntary sale is politically untenable, and force would break NATO treaties.
No US political faction has proposed or built momentum for annexing Greenland territory in 2024-2025, making the short time window even more prohibitive.
sources_consulted: News archives on Trump's 2019 Greenland purchase proposal (Reuters, BBC)
